questions.mathStats:
1. Can we write AB=BA; where A and B are matrices?
2. When can we write AB=BA?
3. Suppose a Constant Matrix A is matrix multiplied with a vector matrix p, then differentiate the expression Ap
4. 2 die are throw one after the other then what is the probability of the expression X+Y+XY to be even if X denotes the outcome of the first dice and Y denotes the outcome of the second die?
questions.logical: 1. For the question number 4 asked above what is the logic gate diagram for X+Y+XY expression?

records.tips:
1. written exam: Most of the questions are fundamental in nature and also question types are repeated every year. Capitalise on the common types and practice a few tough ones as well since cutoff will go extremely high due to competition. I would recommend practising mocks as well as completing the whole syllabus for the exam.
2. interview: Anything goes tbh. You cannot predict the 15 mins allocated to you. Be Confident and get your interview fundamentals right.
Fundamentals include:
Tell Me About Yourself
Why PGDBA
Work ex (if your work ex is in analytics expect heavy questioning here, your interview most likely will run here if you have a analytics background.)
Future Prospects
Strengths and Weaknesses
After Fundamentals get to puzzle solving from Geeks for Geeks, again here is only a few handfuls of patterns available just understand the fundamental logic. Finally, learn linear regression (in-depth) and revise graduation math. Apart from technical aspects, try to complete all the news videos from StudyIQ from January to the Date of your interview in descending order i.e. first complete the current month's news and slowly if time permits work your way towards the old news.

records.tips:

• Avoid beating around the bush; it's okay if you can't answer a few questions.

My preparation also focused on these areas, and I even tried to steer the interview towards math through my intro. However, they asked me mechanical engineering questions instead. If you have a basic understanding of your field, you'll be able to handle those questions as well.

3) It’s ok if you are not able to give 2-3 answers in the interview, just let the panel know that you know the things by giving examples of your field.
4) don’t waste the panelist’s time, just say you don’t know the answer and move to the next question.
5) best luck and don’t panic!
